title: Product Strategy
description: The first two weeks decide the next two years. We pull the idea apart with the people who have to live with it, agree what the first release has to prove, and write down what we are deliberately leaving out.
pointOne: A one-page scope for v1, and the explicit not-doing list beside it
pointTwo: Positioning: who it is for, what it replaces, why now
pointThree: The single metric that decides whether the launch worked
pointFour: A week-by-week plan you could hand to another studio

title: Brand Identity
description: A mark, a typeface, a palette, and a voice — but more usefully, the rules that let your own team apply them without asking permission. We build brands for people who will be using them at 6pm on a Friday.
pointOne: Wordmark and mark, drawn as vectors in every format you need
pointTwo: Type and colour system, specified as design tokens
pointThree: Voice guide with real examples, not adjectives
pointFour: Templates for the ten things you will actually make

title: Product Design
description: Every screen, every state, every edge case — empty, loading, error, and the one nobody thought of. Delivered as a component library your engineers build straight from rather than interpret.
pointOne: The full product designed to the last empty state
pointTwo: A component library in code-ready tokens
pointThree: Prototypes for anything that needed testing on real people
pointFour: Weekly design reviews with whoever is building it

title: Engineering
description: We build the thing. Typed end to end, tested where tests earn their keep, deployed on infrastructure your team can operate after we leave. No framework you have never heard of.
pointOne: A production application in your own repository
pointTwo: CI, staging, and a deploy your team can run
pointThree: Documentation written for the engineer who joins next year
pointFour: A week of pairing at handover, and a month on call after
